answer: The HelloWorldApp is structured around several key components, each encapsulated in its own source code file. The application is orchestrated by the Manager class, which implements the INotifier interface and is responsible for running the application and managing worker instances. The Program class serves as the entry point of the application, where the Main method initializes the Manager and starts the execution process. The application utilizes a factory pattern through the WorkerFactory class to create instances of workers, specifically WorkerA, WorkerB, and WorkerC, all of which implement the IWorker interface. These workers perform tasks and send notifications back to the Manager. The Helper class, located in the HelloWorldApp.Utilities namespace, provides utility functions such as message formatting. The application also includes a TestAliases class for testing purposes. The codebase makes use of external libraries like System and System.Collections.Generic to support its operations.
